summary: Add a factual /roadmap/ page to the private website, marking each platform milestone as built and checked, built but still in testing, or next, with its outstanding work shown beside what exists. Statuses derived from inspected code, guide pages and recorded QA evidence. Published by the maintainer as release 20260911-roadmap and verified against the live backend. Fixes a stale release-copy assertion that failed the website browser check at HEAD (BUG-0071), a shared header navigation that could not wrap (BUG-0072), and a logo assertion that crashed against the deployment's img-src policy (BUG-0073). API impact: none — a prerendered static page with client rendering disabled calls no Controller operation, Core command or client-facing API. The board was then rebuilt as a scannable card layout with status meters and native disclosures after the first version read as a wall of text. Also adds a roadmap impact assessment to the change-record gate so a completed feature cannot land while the published board still calls it unbuilt; both workflows already run that checker, so no workflow file changes.

guide.reason: The website gains a Roadmap page in its navigation, so the preview guide documents the step, what the status marks mean and that no dates are published. The guide index sentence claiming VM editing is unavailable was corrected: editing is implemented and already has its own guide page.

api.reason: A prerendered static page with csr = false. Browser navigation fetches static files only; there is no Controller operation, Core agent command, observed-state or result flow, and no client-facing service API. The browser check exercises the built output, so no API tests apply and the API reference is unchanged.

roadmap.reason: This change creates the published roadmap board itself and sets every milestone's status from inspected code, guide pages and recorded QA evidence.

state.reason: Website source and its verification evidence only. The page holds no Nex Controller or Core state; it describes milestone status, and the authority for that status remains the platform plan and the host-side records the plan already defines.

verification.method: svelte-check 0 errors/0 warnings across 266 files and a clean static build. The website browser walkthrough passed all 12 groups at 1440, 768 and 360 pixels and with JavaScript disabled, covering roadmap navigation, the status legend, a status pill and list items per milestone, the presence of both built and outstanding lists, the keyboard skip link, no horizontal overflow and no media download links — first against a locally served build, then against the live private backend after the maintainer published release 20260911-roadmap. Before publishing, the deployed index.html was confirmed byte-identical to a build of HEAD; after publishing, all 13 served files matched the build manifest by SHA-256. nginx returned 200 for /roadmap/, 404 for an unknown path and 403 for a directory, with the strict CSP, HSTS, nosniff, DENY and no-referrer headers present. Local, mobile and deployed captures were inspected. BUG-0071 was reproduced at HEAD before any change, BUG-0072 at 360px, and BUG-0073 against the deployed backend; all three fixed and re-run. Milestone statuses were checked against internal/, cmd/, web/src/, docs/guide/ and docs/qa/ rather than plan headings; phases 4 to 10 confirmed unimplemented by source inspection. Not done: the Pangolin HTTPS route and access policy, rollback rehearsal, and independent review. The roadmap assessment is covered by four new checker tests (missing field on a new record, updated-without-a-board-change, pages outside the board area, and records predating the field staying valid); the suite passes 25 tests and check_docs.py --all still passes against all existing records with no retrofit. After the presentation rebuild, svelte-check, the build and all 12 browser groups were re-run and pass; the keyboard-expanded card state and desktop/mobile captures were inspected.
